# Add the greeting module boundary contract

## Problem Statement

The greeting fixture currently exports only `greet`. The existing validators require a canonical `FAREWELL` export with the value `"bye"` and an exact public export surface of `greet` and `FAREWELL`. The requested downstream usage module does not yet exist.

## Desired Outcome

Expose the required farewell value from the canonical greeting module, add a small module that re-exports that value, and retain the exact public contract expected by the fixture validators.

## Scope

- Add the declaration-style named export `FAREWELL` with value `"bye"` to `src/greeting.mjs`, preserving `greet`.
- Add `src/usage.mjs` as a downstream re-export of `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs`.
- Extend the contract validator to cover the downstream re-export.
- Run the required fixture and contract validators, plus the source architecture check.

## Non-goals

- Change the behavior or signature of `greet`.
- Add any other public export to `src/greeting.mjs`.
- Add a dependency or alter package configuration.

## Observable Behavior

This change does alter externally observable behavior: consumers can import `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs` and from the new `src/usage.mjs`.

## Assumptions

The usage module will be named `src/usage.mjs`. The explorer evidence shows that `src/format.mjs` activates conditional architecture rules and would conflict with the required one-way re-export from greeting.

# Design: greeting module boundary

## Approach

Keep `src/greeting.mjs` as the canonical source. Preserve its existing `greet` function and add the declaration-style export `export const FAREWELL = "bye"`. Add `src/usage.mjs` with a one-way re-export of `FAREWELL` from `./greeting.mjs`; do not duplicate the value or add an import in the opposite direction.

## Repository Boundaries

- `src/greeting.mjs` remains the validated public module and exposes exactly `greet` and `FAREWELL`.
- `src/usage.mjs` is a downstream usage layer and re-exports only `FAREWELL`.
- `scripts/contract.mjs` will assert that the usage-layer import resolves to `"bye"`, closing the current coverage gap for that module.
- Do not name the new module `src/format.mjs`; its existence activates architecture checks that conflict with importing `./greeting.mjs`.

## Compatibility and Risks

The public API gains one named export. The value and existing `greet` behavior are constrained by current validators. Extra exports on `src/greeting.mjs` fail the exact-surface contract. No schema, dependency, or package API changes are needed.

## Validation

Run `node scripts/validate.mjs`, `node scripts/contract.mjs`, and `node scripts/architecture.mjs`. The first two are the explicit required fixture gates; the architecture check also verifies the declaration-style exact source surface.

artifacts.proposal:
# Add the greeting module boundary contract

## Problem Statement

The greeting fixture currently exports only `greet`. The existing validators require a canonical `FAREWELL` export with the value `"bye"` and an exact public export surface of `greet` and `FAREWELL`. The requested downstream usage module does not yet exist.

## Desired Outcome

Expose the required farewell value from the canonical greeting module, add a small module that re-exports that value, and retain the exact public contract expected by the fixture validators.

## Scope

- Add the declaration-style named export `FAREWELL` with value `"bye"` to `src/greeting.mjs`, preserving `greet`.
- Add `src/usage.mjs` as a downstream re-export of `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs`.
- Extend the contract validator to cover the downstream re-export.
- Run the required fixture and contract validators, plus the source architecture check.

## Non-goals

- Change the behavior or signature of `greet`.
- Add any other public export to `src/greeting.mjs`.
- Add a dependency or alter package configuration.

## Observable Behavior

This change does alter externally observable behavior: consumers can import `FAREWELL` from `src/greeting.mjs` and from the new `src/usage.mjs`.

## Assumptions

The usage module will be named `src/usage.mjs`. The explorer evidence shows that `src/format.mjs` activates conditional architecture rules and would conflict with the required one-way re-export from greeting.
artifacts.design:
# Design: greeting module boundary

## Approach

Keep `src/greeting.mjs` as the canonical source. Preserve its existing `greet` function and add the declaration-style export `export const FAREWELL = "bye"`. Add `src/usage.mjs` with a one-way re-export of `FAREWELL` from `./greeting.mjs`; do not duplicate the value or add an import in the opposite direction.

## Repository Boundaries

- `src/greeting.mjs` remains the validated public module and exposes exactly `greet` and `FAREWELL`.
- `src/usage.mjs` is a downstream usage layer and re-exports only `FAREWELL`.
- `scripts/contract.mjs` will assert that the usage-layer import resolves to `"bye"`, closing the current coverage gap for that module.
- Do not name the new module `src/format.mjs`; its existence activates architecture checks that conflict with importing `./greeting.mjs`.

## Compatibility and Risks

The public API gains one named export. The value and existing `greet` behavior are constrained by current validators. Extra exports on `src/greeting.mjs` fail the exact-surface contract. No schema, dependency, or package API changes are needed.

## Validation

Run `node scripts/validate.mjs`, `node scripts/contract.mjs`, and `node scripts/architecture.mjs`. The first two are the explicit required fixture gates; the architecture check also verifies the declaration-style exact source surface.
